summary:
I try to make software a bit more usable and respectful of its users, which, to no one's surprise, makes me most passionate about Linux, open-source, and usable privacy even in the uncertain age of AI. 

In general, I have a strong preference for research / R&D, open-source, and academia. I have experience in large-scale distributed systems and low-level systems engineering, with my formal specialization being in HPC and distributed systems engineering, and a minor in Machine Learning acquired at Carnegie Mellon University.

positions.title: Visiting Researcher
positions.description:
Designed novel hardware-software codesign solution for fault-tolerant memory safety on RISC-V architecture. Extended Linux kernel, bootloader (U-Boot), and glibc to enable tunable dynamic memory safety with zero overhead for legal executions.

- Implemented FTMS (Fault-Tolerant Memory Safety) framework correcting Out-Of-Bounds and Use-After-Free errors
- Achieved memory safety enforcement with minimal performance penalty on legal operations vs standard RISC-V builds
- Demonstrated availability restoration in real-world benchmark tests under memory corruption scenarios
- Extended multiple layers of the software stack: kernel, bootloader, C library allocator

(Tech: RISC-V, C/C++, Linux kernel, glibc, hardware-software codesign, memory safety)
